meta.title: Awesome Showreels
meta.reviewed: Draft from extract_style.py run on the repository README (v1.1.0 text and badges, frozen in source/readme-v1.1.0.md), reviewed by hand: see rationale; the extraction log is style-extract.md.

source.notes: the repository README at v1.1.0 (commit 9c19853), text and badges only: its relative image links are left unresolved on purpose, so the previews this project renders never feed back into its own style

rationale.palette: Dark theme. The README's only authored colours are its six badge colours, picked by hex: #F5C2E7, #CBA6F7, #89B4FA, #94E2D5, #A6E3A1, #FAB387 [E10]. They are exactly Catppuccin Mocha's pink, mauve, blue, teal, green and peach, and the README names Catppuccin as the terminal palette of its CC-statusline case study, so the reel takes the whole Mocha family. The extractor's bg #0A0E17 came from a table cell that describes the research-cli example [E6] (a hex in a comparison table describes something else), so it is replaced by Mocha's own darkest stage, crust #11111B; bg2 mantle #181825, surface base #1E1E2E, line surface0 #313244, ink text #CDD6F4 (12.97:1), ink2 subtext0 #A6ADC8 (8.42:1), muted overlay2 #9399B2 (6.64:1 on bg, 5.81:1 on surface; the draft's #777B82 was replaced by the family's own grey). accent mauve #CBA6F7 (the 'Claude Code skill + plugin' badge, the product's identity, 9.23:1), accent2 pink #F5C2E7 (stars badge), accent3 blue #89B4FA (output badge); ok green #A6E3A1 (narration badge), warn Mocha yellow #F9E2AF, deny Mocha red #F38BA8; the remaining badge colours stay available as extra keys teal #94E2D5 (music badge) and orange #FAB387 (Mocha's peach, the licence badge; the runtime reserves the key name peach for a derived tint). ok and deny are close for deutan viewers: the reel pairs them with marks and words. paletteAlt is Catppuccin Latte, the sibling light theme (unused: every scene is dark).
rationale.type: The README declares no font: GitHub sets it in the system UI face with code in a monospace face. Every frame must render the same pixels on any machine, so the reel uses embeddable faces that already ship in this repository under the SIL OFL 1.1: Space Grotesk for display and body (a grotesk with mono-derived details, between the README's prose and its code blocks) and JetBrains Mono for labels, numbers and code (the README is 34 code-like tokens per 1k words [E1]). The extractor's draft set the display role in mono and the body in Inter, which is not installed everywhere. Nunito is loaded only to set the playful-app example's own type specimen. displayWeight 700, bodyWeight 500 (light text on a dark stage, downscaled for README previews, needs a little weight); headline tracking -0.02 em; labels tracked 0.14 em, in caps, like the README's section kickers.
rationale.motion: Energy 0.46: 11.46 emoji per 1k words but almost no '!' or marketing words, 39.64 numbers per 1k [E1] → medium pace; playful 0.34, technical 0.84 → spring f 2.25 z 0.67 with a visible but short overshoot (0.7), ease outExpo: confident, not bouncy. Transitions from the tone scores: glitch 0.67, zoomInto 0.67, match 0.55, whip 0.40, impact 0.37 (used by the tour cut). Corners stay tight (radius 12, chips 8): the README's badges are flat-square [E10].
rationale.sound: dark-synth scored 0.72 (next lofi 0.40) from dark 1, technical 0.84, playful 0.34. The draft's 124 BPM (inside 118–130 by energy) is nudged to 120: a bar is exactly 2.0 s, so every 3-bar README loop is a whole number of frames at 20, 24 or 25 fps and loops without a seam. Key Db from the accent hue 309° (free choice), minor; drums full; sfx digital. Only the 36-s tour cut has a soundtrack; the README previews are silent.
rationale.narration: Off. The draft recommended narration for an explainer, but these loops autoplay muted inside a README and carry their message in type; a voice would need the viewer's own Gemini key (BYOK) and an audio track that animated WebP cannot hold. Captions are off for the same reason.
rationale.visuals: The README is a technical tool page with 4 tables and 6 shell commands [E1] and no mascot of its own (characters false). Every carrier on screen is the bundled examples' real material: style boards, README renders, the Mochi mascot lifted from the playful-app logo by Vision with a blink twin, the real app UI captures, the real spark-bench CLI cast, cut plans, music and captions computed by the skill, and the real HTML player. Post: grain 0, because per-frame grain multiplies the size of an animated WebP; a static vignette and a light bloom keep the stage cinematic.
